standing: Author correction for review finding PS-04. Selects the smallest sufficient anchor for report asset bytes and defines its private descriptors and validation. Not an accepted amendment, not executable product code, not a wire schema and not acceptance of frozen candidate25 bytes. Requires its own substantive review on newly frozen bytes.

correctionOf.withdrawnClaim: The host release's existing authenticated artifact/catalog association commits an exact asset-manifest regular file and every asset member.
correctionOf.reason: Verified unsupported against frozen candidate25. The only published per-file TreeCommitment path is the DR-103 component manifest, whose manifestSchema kind is a closed enum with initial vocabulary 'component'; the TR-INDEX-signed catalog releases[].artifacts[] row commits only {platform, archiveProfileId, archiveDigest, sha256} and no per-member listing; and the signed core release manifest schema2 that would carry release-side bindings is described in S9.1 as prospective, with CoreProfileBindingV2 carrying two members. No host-release per-member listing is published anywhere in the frozen bytes.
correctionOf.remedy: Anchor load-time asset integrity in a compile-time constant inside the already-trusted host binary. Keep install-time provenance where it already lives. Introduce no closure2 kind, no manifest wire schema, no per-file signing metadata and no new D9 code.

frozenSourceAnchors.fact: Signed software provenance does not prove that an algorithm is correct; the selected, authenticated first-party host and pure evaluator remain in the TCB. The running host bytes are therefore already trusted by the selected trust model.

Under a schema-1 root a standalone platform-profile-set document is refused typed and only the copy embedded in the signed core release (TR-CORE namespace) is used. Embedding trusted metadata in the signed core release and preferring the embedded copy over a standalone document is therefore an established pattern in the frozen design, not an invention of this correction.

TR-CORE is a required root role in both closed root schemas, alongside TR-INDEX, TR-COMPONENT, TR-BUNDLE, TR-REPAIR and (schema 2) TR-PROFILE. TR-CORE, not TR-COMPONENT, is the applicable CORE/host release owner.

The prospective signed core release manifest schema2 carries required platformProfileBinding. It is explicitly prospective, and a stage-2 reader ships under the old schema-1 release first. No core release manifest shape, and no per-member core release listing, is published in frozen bytes.

The published per-file identity path is the DR-103 component-manifest delivery selector component-manifest-schemas.v11 manifestSchema.platforms[] (os, arch, tree TreeCommitment, entrypoint) with RJ-3, whose closure.tree projects type=file rows onto identity Blob {path, sha256, bytes}. The TR-INDEX-signed catalog row is opensip-catalog.1 releases[] {manifestDigest, manifestPreimageSha256, envelopeDigest, artifacts[{platform, archiveProfileId, archiveDigest, sha256}]}.

The closure2 kind enum has exactly eight members: provider, evaluator, detector, toolchain, stdlib, rust-dev-llvm, grammar, adapter. There is no host or asset kind, and the substring platform-independent does not occur in that schema.

frozenSourceAnchors.selector: G3 physical substrate, line 347, and egress defaults, line 346
frozenSourceAnchors.fact: The selected substrate includes the signed offline assets required for the authoritative profile; every physical dependency actually used belongs to the admitted closure/TCB inventory and its packaging/offline/quality gates; missing assets never trigger ambient downloads or a weaker analyzer; ordinary analysis and discovery are offline with no implicit refresh, download or required egress.

frozenSourceAnchors.selector: lines 829-842 and the golden table rows at 988-990
frozenSourceAnchors.fact: A missing field or projection exception is a required-delivery operational fault: operational-failed, exit 4, faultCause=delivery-required, DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED; if a Run was already committed the termination retains its RunId, otherwise no RunId is invented. Installed closure bytes corrupt is operational-failed 4 HOST.IO_FAILURE with detail DELIVERY.CLOSURE_BYTES_CORRUPT. Selected renderer fails after commit is operational-failed 4 DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED with detail DELIVERY.RENDERER_FAILED_AFTER_COMMIT and runId retained. An optional export sink failure is success 0.
closed is true. DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED and HOST.IO_FAILURE are both existing errorCodes members. This correction mints no code and uses only members of that closed vocabulary.
A coherent rollback of the entire install root with the marker suppressed is stated as not detected. Whole-install-root substitution is already outside local detection.

anchorSelection.selected: compile-time host-embedded pin over the exact private asset manifest bytes
anchorSelection.statement: The host binary carries a build-embedded constant HostAssetPinV1 holding the raw SHA-256 and exact byte length of the private ReportAssetManifestV1 document that shipped with it. At load, reporting/assets.rs reads the supplied manifest bytes, checks length then digest against that constant, and only then validates each selected asset member against the manifest. Nothing outside the host binary needs to be signed for this check to hold.
whySufficient: Trust reduces to trust in the host bytes, which anchor B1 already places in the TCB. The code that would verify any signature lives in the same binary as the pin, so per-file signing over an install root cannot be stronger than the binary that checks it.

Anchor B10 already states that whole-install-root substitution is undetected locally. Adding per-file signing metadata inside that same install root does not move that boundary; it only adds a wire schema and a signing ceremony.
Anchor B2 shows the frozen design already prefers a copy embedded in the signed core release over a standalone document for exactly this class of trusted metadata.
It is fully offline: no catalog lookup, no network, no package manager, no filesystem search outside the release-relative asset root. This satisfies anchor B7 directly.
It introduces no closure2 kind (B6), no component or core manifest schema (B4, B5), no signature-envelope kind and no public major.

whatItDoesNotCover.installTimeProvenance: The pin says nothing about where the host binary came from. Provenance of the delivered core release archive remains with the existing signing chain: TR-CORE as the core release root role (B3), distributed through the TR-INDEX-signed catalog whose artifacts[] row commits archiveDigest and sha256 for each platform archive (B5). Assets ship inside that archive and are covered transitively by its archive digest.
whatItDoesNotCover.honestDependency: The exact catalog row shape for a CORE release, as opposed to the component release row quoted in B5, is NOT published in frozen candidate25, and the core release manifest schema2 is explicitly prospective (B4). This correction does not assert that a published core-release row exists. Load-time asset integrity, which is what report rendering actually needs, does not depend on it.
whatItDoesNotCover.dependencyOwner: Completing the core release manifest and its catalog row belongs to the release and carrier work that is separately active. If that owner later publishes a core release manifest, binding assetManifestSha256 into it is a strictly additive audit convenience, not a prerequisite for this design.
whatItDoesNotCover.notClaimed: No claim is made that a prospective record is published, that report assets are a producer, that they enter any semantic Run identity, or that asset packaging changes native context.

rejectedAlternatives.option: A ninth closure2.kind for report assets
rejectedAlternatives.rejected: B6: the kind enum is closed at eight members and assets produce no evidence. This was already rejected in the reviewed package and remains rejected.

rejectedAlternatives.option: Reuse the DR-103 component manifest platforms[].tree TreeCommitment for the host release
rejectedAlternatives.rejected: B5 plus the closed manifestSchema kind vocabulary 'component'. Using it for a host release needs a kind vocabulary successor and a core release manifest that B4 says is prospective. That is a larger owner change than the problem requires.

rejectedAlternatives.option: A new per-file signed asset manifest with its own signature-envelope kind
rejectedAlternatives.rejected: It would add a signed wire schema, a root role or namespace decision and a signing ceremony, to protect bytes inside an install root whose wholesale substitution B10 already declares undetected, verified by code in a binary that B1 already trusts.
B7: ordinary analysis is offline with no implicit refresh. Rendering must not depend on catalog availability.

HostAssetPinV1.what: The build-embedded constant compiled into the host binary. Not a file the host reads, not caller input, not serialized on any wire.
HostAssetPinV1.owningModule: crates/reporting/src/assets.rs holds the constant and performs the check; the value is supplied by the explicit build/release input the plan's asset policy already requires.

assetRoot.description: Release-tree-relative directory holding the asset members. Canonical POSIX relative path: no leading slash, no . or .. segment, no backslash, no NUL, no trailing slash.

assetManifestPath.description: Release-tree-relative path of the ReportAssetManifestV1 regular file, under assetRoot, subject to the same canonical-path rule.

assetManifestSha256.description: Raw SHA-256 of the exact manifest bytes as stored. Not a canonicalized digest and not H(domain, descriptor); this is a raw-artifact digest over stored bytes, the same representation class as the frozen SyntaxGrammarBundleV1.bundleDigest.

assetManifestBytes.description: Exact stored byte length, checked before the digest so a read is length-bounded. This mirrors the frozen BLOB_LENGTH discipline in which retained blob length must match.

buildChannel.description: development marks a build pinned over labelled fixture assets. A development build must state its channel in version output and can never present itself as a signed product release.

ReportAssetManifestV1.what: The private asset manifest document that ships in the release tree. Unchanged in shape from the reviewed package; restated here as a closed schema so the pin and the checks have an exact subject.
ReportAssetManifestV1.owningModule: produced by report build assembly; validated by crates/reporting/src/assets.rs

projectionSchemaSha256s.description: Raw SHA-256 of each complete supported report projection schema document. Ascending byte order, nonempty, unique.

assets.description: Regular-file rows only, ascending by path in byte order, globally unique paths.

extraAdmissionRules: Every path is release-tree-relative and canonical: no leading slash, no . or .. segment, no backslash, no NUL byte, no trailing slash, no duplicate path.
Every path must lie under the pin's assetRoot.

Rows are regular files only. A directory, symlink or device at a listed path refuses; no symlink is ever followed. This mirrors the frozen identity rule that type=dir and type=symlink stay delivery rows and are never followed into a listing.
The list is sorted ascending by path in byte order and the sort is checked, not assumed.
No URL, scheme, authority or network reference may appear in any member.
Unknown member, duplicate JSON key, implicit default or lossy numeric parse refuses.
License and notice files are exact retained members with role notice; they are required delivery content, not optional decoration.

buildTimeValidation.owner: report build assembly, then release assembly
steps: Emit ReportAssetManifestV1 over the exact built asset bytes, with real lengths and raw SHA-256 values, sorted and unique.
Verify every listed member exists as a regular file under assetRoot with the listed length and digest, and that no unlisted regular file exists under assetRoot.
Compute assetManifestSha256 and assetManifestBytes over the manifest bytes as stored, and compile them into the host binary as HostAssetPinV1 with buildChannel release.
Refuse assembly, per the plan's existing rule, if the selected report asset bundle is missing or incompatible.
prohibited: No ambient package-manager invocation and no network fetch at any point, including from a Cargo build script.
No producer identity, closure2 kind or component manifest is created for report assets.
A development build may pin labelled fixture assets only with buildChannel development.

loadTimeValidation.precondition: Performed only when an asset-consuming renderer has been selected for the admitted command. Absence or corruption of report assets never affects a human, JSON, agent or SARIF invocation, and never changes analysis, admission or any verdict.
orderedSteps: Resolve assetManifestPath under assetRoot relative to the installed release tree, through safe handles with no symlink traversal and no path supplied by a caller, request, environment variable or configuration file.
Read at most assetManifestBytes plus one byte; refuse if the stored length differs from assetManifestBytes.
Compute raw SHA-256 of the exact stored bytes and require byte equality with assetManifestSha256. Refuse on any difference.
Parse the manifest under the closed schema and the extra admission rules. Refuse on any violation.
Require the selected report projection schema digest to be a member of projectionSchemaSha256s. A projection the shipped assets do not support is an incompatibility, not a silent downgrade.
For each asset member the selected renderer will consume, read it under its listed length, compute its raw SHA-256 and require byte equality. Refuse on any difference.
Only then may html_renderer.rs and html_embedding.rs consume the bytes.
loadTimeValidation.authorityBoundary: Trust and installation remain with lifecycle and security. assets.rs performs an integrity check against a constant compiled into the binary it is part of; it admits no trust, reads no catalog, verifies no signature and grants nothing.

failureBehavior.vocabulary: Only existing closed D9 v1.14 members are used (anchor B9). No code, class, exit or detail is minted.

cases.case: Required asset validation fails and no Run has been committed
cases.basis: B8: a required output that cannot be produced is a required-delivery operational fault, and otherwise no RunId is invented.

cases.case: Required asset validation fails after a Run was already committed
cases.basis: B8: the selected renderer failing after commit keeps its RunId and the after-commit detail. Assurance and verdict of the committed Run are unchanged.

cases.case: An optional surface only, for example an optional browser launch or optional export, cannot use the assets
cases.basis: B8: an optional sink failure is disclosed without changing the sealed result.
Asset validation is not performed; see loadTimeValidation.precondition.

neverDone: Never render a partial or degraded report from unverified bytes.
Never fetch, regenerate or substitute a missing asset.
Never downgrade a required HTML request to another format to avoid the fault.
Never treat an asset fault as an analysis, coverage or policy result.

limits: The pin is exactly as trustworthy as the host binary that carries it. That is the selected trust model (B1), not an improvement on it.
Whole-install-root substitution, including replacing the binary and its assets together, is not detected locally. That is the existing stated bound (B10).

This correction establishes load-time integrity only. Install-time provenance of the delivered archive stays with TR-CORE and the existing catalog chain, whose exact CORE row shape is not published in frozen candidate25 and is named here as an open dependency of the separately active release and carrier work.
No product code is authored. Owning modules are named for implementation planning only.
This is a proposed design correction on unfrozen author bytes. It is not accepted, confers no readiness, and requires an independent substantive review.
Browser behavior, offline rendering and accessibility remain unqualified; source-level asset binding establishes none of them.
